packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut: The extension point for computing attribute values. Other plugins (and the plugin itself) supply `AttributeLoaderProvider` components that turn an `AttributeSpec` into an `AttributeLoader`; the loader kinds here (item, derived, single-row, aggregate, propagate, scanning) differ in what data a value may depend on, and the context interfaces are what the plugin hands to loaders while it calculates. It also holds the trail model (`TrailItemSet`) used for cache invalidation.

Ready-made abstract base classes and a few concrete loaders (sums, inherited values, simple derivations) that make writing attribute loaders easier, plus a minimal `AttributeLoaderProvider` implementation that serves a fixed set of loaders.

Fluent builders that create attribute loaders from lambdas (item, derived, single-row), and the loader classes those builders produce. Normally reached through the static factory methods of `AttributeLoaders` / `SharedAttributeLoaders`.

Support for combining several loaders that serve the same attribute into one composite loader, including adapting a simpler loader kind to a more general one, and the `LoaderType` classification of loader kinds.
Base classes for loaders that wrap another loader of the same kind and forward every call to it; subclass to override selected behaviour.

Aggregate loaders that compute a row's value by reducing the values of its subtree, with pluggable reduction strategies (whole subtree, children only, leaves only, strict subtree) selected by the attribute spec's `type` parameter.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Context passed to an `AggregateAttributeLoader` while it computes the value for one row; in addition to the row it exposes the row's direct children. Instances are created by the plugin for one loading request and are only valid during the call they are passed to; do not keep or share them across threads.

members.getChildren(): The direct children of the current row in the forest being calculated, in forest order. The list has the same size and order as the list of child values passed to `AggregateAttributeLoader.loadValue`. Empty for a leaf row; never null. Read-only. If the loader is not allowed to access items, the rows returned refuse to resolve their items.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Extension-point loader kind for values that depend on the row's subtree (totals, counts and the like). The plugin calculates children before parents and calls the loader once per row with the already computed values of the row's direct children. Implemented by plugins and returned from an `AttributeLoaderProvider`. As a multi-row loader its default caching strategy is `SHOULD`.

members.loadValue(java.util.List, com.almworks.j: Computes the value for the row given by `context.getRow()`. Argument 1: the values already computed for the row's direct children, one entry per child in the same order as `context.getChildren()` (entries are never null; missing values are undefined values). Argument 2: the aggregate context. Returns the value; returning null is treated by the plugin as an undefined value (inside a composite loader null means 'not handled, try the next loader'). A runtime exception thrown here is logged and turned into an error value for that row.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Tells the plugin whether the values produced by a loader may be kept in its value cache between requests. Returned by `AttributeLoader.getCachingStrategy()`. A dependency's `MUST_NOT` is inherited by every attribute that depends on it.

members.SHOULD: Values are expensive to compute and should be cached. Default for multi-row loaders (aggregate, propagate, scanning).
members.MAY: Values may be cached; computing them again is also acceptable. Default for loaders whose spec uses one of the standard value formats.
members.SHOULD_NOT: Values should not be stored in the value cache (each request recomputes them), though the plugin still keeps invalidation tracking for them. Default for non-standard value formats.
members.MUST_NOT: Values must never be cached, and nothing derived from them may be cached either: every attribute that depends on such an attribute is also treated as `MUST_NOT`.
members.guessCachingStrategy(com.almworks.jira.s: Default strategy for a spec when a loader does not state one: `MAY` if the spec's value format is one of the standard formats known to `ValueFormat` (looked up by format id), otherwise `SHOULD_NOT`. The argument must not be null (NullPointerException).

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Base context available to loaders and providers during attribute calculation: who the values are computed for, locale and time zone, the time of the request, the base structure, and a per-request scratch map for sharing objects between loaders. Implemented only by the plugin. When called by a loader, several getters verify that the loader declared the matching `AttributeContextDependency`; calling them without it throws IllegalStateException (if the dependency is only inherited from an attribute dependency, a warning is logged instead). When called from an `AttributeLoaderProvider` while the loader is being created, the same getters instead mark the provider's loader as not reusable and record the dependency as implied. Instances are created by the plugin for one loading request and are only valid during the call they are passed to; do not keep or share them across threads.

members.getUser(): The user on whose behalf values are calculated, or null for an anonymous user. Requires the `USER` context dependency.
members.getI18nHelper(): Jira's `I18nHelper` for the calculating user's locale. Requires `USER_LOCALE` (or `USER`). Never null.
members.getI18n(): The plugin's `I18n` text helper for the calculating user's locale, backed by the same Jira helper. Never null. Note: unlike `getI18nHelper()`, the plugin does not check context dependencies here.
members.getLocale(): The calculating user's locale (as reported by the user's `I18nHelper`). Requires `USER_LOCALE` (or `USER`). Never null.
members.getTimeZone(): The calculating user's time zone as configured in Jira. Requires `USER_TIMEZONE` (or `USER`). Never null.
members.getBaseStructureId(): Id of the structure on whose forest the values are being calculated, or 0 when the calculation is not tied to a structure. Requires the `STRUCTURE` context dependency.
members.getLoadTimeMillis(): Wall-clock time (milliseconds since the epoch) captured when the loading request began; the same for every value computed in that request, so use it instead of the system clock. Requires `CURRENT_TIME`.
members.getLoadTimeNanos(): Value of the JVM's monotonic nanosecond timer captured when the loading request began; only meaningful for measuring intervals within this JVM. Requires `CURRENT_TIME`.
members.getBaseUrl(): Jira's configured base URL without a trailing slash, or an empty string if none is configured. Never null.
members.putObject(Object, Object): Stores an object under a key in a scratch map that lives as long as the loading request and is shared by all loaders called in it (useful for request-level caches). Argument 1: the key (not null). Argument 2: the value; null removes the key. Throws IllegalArgumentException for keys that are reserved by the export framework (the keys defined in `ExportContextKeys`), which are read-only to loaders.
members.getObject(Object): Returns the object stored under the key in the request's scratch map (by `putObject` or by the plugin, e.g. export keys from `ExportContextKeys`), cast to the caller's expected type; null if absent. The cast is unchecked, so a wrong expected type fails at the caller.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Kinds of context information (besides attribute dependencies and the item/row itself) a loader's values may depend on. A loader declares them through `AttributeLoader.getContextDependencies()`; the plugin keys cached values by the declared dimensions (for example, per user) and refuses context getters for undeclared ones. Declaring `USER` implies `USER_LOCALE` and `USER_TIMEZONE`.

members.USER: Values depend on the calculating user (permissions, user-specific data). Cached values are kept per user. Implies locale and time zone.
members.USER_LOCALE: Values depend on the calculating user's locale (e.g. localised text) but not otherwise on the user.
members.USER_TIMEZONE: Values depend on the calculating user's time zone (e.g. date formatting or day boundaries).
members.STRUCTURE: Values depend on which structure is being calculated (see `AttributeContext.getBaseStructureId()`); cached values are kept per structure.
members.CURRENT_TIME: Values depend on the current time. Required to call the load-time getters and `AttributeLoaderContext.valueExpires`; such values expire and are periodically recalculated.
members.TRAIL: The loader reports trails (`AttributeLoaderContext.addTrail`): its values depend on items other than the row's own item, and change to those items must invalidate them.
members.guessContextDependencies(com.almworks.ji: Default context dependencies for a spec when a loader does not state them: a set containing only `USER` if the spec's format is the HTML format (`ValueFormat.HTML`), otherwise null (no context dependencies). The argument must not be null.
members.union(java.util.Set, com.almworks.jira.s: Returns a new, mutable set holding all elements of the given set plus the additional dependencies. Argument 1 may be null (treated as empty); the varargs array and its null elements are ignored. Never returns null; the arguments are not modified.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Base interface of all attribute loaders: an object that computes values of exactly one attribute spec. Loaders are created by `AttributeLoaderProvider` implementations (usually from the builders in `AttributeLoaders`) and then used by the plugin, possibly from several threads and for many requests, so implementations should be stateless or thread-safe. A loader must implement exactly one of the concrete kinds (`ItemAttributeLoader`, `DerivedAttributeLoader`, `SingleRowAttributeLoader`, `AggregateAttributeLoader`, `PropagateAttributeLoader`, `ScanningAttributeLoader`); the getters here describe what the values depend on and are read once, when the plugin assembles the loader.

members.getAttributeSpec(): The attribute spec this loader computes values for. Never null. It should equal the spec the provider was asked for (a spec with a subset of its parameters and a convertible format is also accepted and adapted by the plugin); otherwise the plugin discards the loader with a warning.
members.getAttributeDependencies(): Specs of other attributes whose values this loader reads through `AttributeLoaderContext.getDependencyAttributeValue`. The plugin loads them first and rejects reading any spec not listed here. Null or empty means no dependencies (default: null). Circular dependencies make the attribute unavailable.
members.getContextDependencies(): Context information the values depend on (see `AttributeContextDependency`). Null means 'not declared' and is treated like an empty set; the default returns `AttributeContextDependency.guessContextDependencies(getAttributeSpec())`.
members.getCachingStrategy(): How the plugin may cache the loader's values; null means no preference. Default: `AttributeCachingStrategy.guessCachingStrategy(getAttributeSpec())`.
members.getGlobalTrail(): Items whose change must invalidate every cached value of this attribute, regardless of row (for example a configuration object the attribute reads). Null (the default) means none. A non-null global trail also disables the plugin's shortcut of re-validating cached values without recomputation.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Context for loaders that compute values: adds access to the values of declared attribute dependencies and lets the loader report trails and expiration for the value being computed. Implemented only by the plugin. Instances are created by the plugin for one loading request and are only valid during the call they are passed to; do not keep or share them across threads.

members.getDependencyAttributeValue(com.almworks: Returns the already computed value of a dependency attribute for the current item or row. The spec must be one of the loader's declared `getAttributeDependencies()`, otherwise IllegalArgumentException. Never returns null: a missing value is an undefined value; if the current row is hidden from the user and the loader is a sensitive multi-row loader, the result is an inaccessible value. If an item-level loader asks for a dependency that needs the forest (a row-based attribute), IllegalArgumentException is thrown. Reading a dependency also makes the current value expire no later than the dependency's value.
members.getDependencyValue(com.almworks.jira.str: Shortcut for the plain value of `getDependencyAttributeValue(dependency)`; null when that value is undefined, an error or otherwise has no value. Same exceptions.
members.addTrail(com.almworks.jira.structure.api: Records that the value being computed also depends on the given items, so that a change to any of them invalidates this value. Calls accumulate (union) for the current value. Null or an empty set is ignored. Requires the `TRAIL` context dependency (IllegalStateException otherwise).
Same as `addTrail(TrailItemSet.of(item))`: records a single item the value depends on. Null is ignored. Reporting the current item itself is pointless (the plugin logs a warning).
Declares that the value being computed becomes stale after the given time, measured from the start of the request. Argument 1: the time to live, must be positive (IllegalArgumentException otherwise). Argument 2: its unit. Several calls (and dependencies' own expirations) keep the earliest expiry. Requires the `CURRENT_TIME` context dependency (IllegalStateException otherwise).

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Extension point through which plugins contribute attributes: given a requested attribute spec, a provider returns a loader for it or null if it does not serve that spec. Implementations are registered as plugin modules/components; the plugin asks every registered provider each time it needs a loader for a spec it has not assembled yet, and combines all loaders returned for the same spec into one composite loader (see `CompositeAttributeLoader`). Assembled loaders are cached and reused for later requests unless the provider called `AttributeProviderContext.mustNotCacheLoader()` or used user-dependent context while creating the loader.

Returns a loader for the spec (argument 1), or null if this provider does not support it. Argument 2 gives the request context (user, locale and so on); using it makes the created loader request-specific. The returned loader's spec should equal the requested spec (a more general spec with fewer parameters and a convertible format is also accepted). Throwing `StructureProviderException` signals that the spec is recognised but cannot be served; the plugin logs it and continues with other providers, as it also does for runtime exceptions.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Static entry point for creating loaders with builders. Adds Jira-issue specific factories to the general ones inherited from `SharedAttributeLoaders`. Not instantiable.

Starts a builder for an item loader of the given spec that supports only Jira issues (item type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue`) and resolves each item to a Jira `Issue`. Use `valueFunction`/`valueFunctionAV` on it; because the item class is preset, the identity-based value functions (`valueFunctionII`, `valueFunctionIIAV`) make `build()` fail with IllegalArgumentException.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Context passed to `AttributeLoaderProvider.createAttributeLoader`. Besides the general context it lets the provider influence whether the created loader may be reused, and query the kind of other attributes. Implemented only by the plugin. Instances are created by the plugin for one loading request and are only valid during the call they are passed to; do not keep or share them across threads.

members.mustNotCacheLoader(): Tells the plugin not to reuse the loader created in this call for later requests (it will ask the providers again next time). The plugin does this automatically when the provider reads user, locale, time zone, structure or time information from the context.
members.isItemAttribute(com.almworks.jira.struct: True if the given attribute's values depend only on the item (not on the row's position in a forest), i.e. it is computed by item loaders or by derived loaders over such attributes. False for null and for row-based attributes. Throws IllegalArgumentException if the check recurses into the attribute currently being checked.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Context passed to a `DerivedAttributeLoader`. Adds nothing to `AttributeLoaderContext`: a derived value may only use dependency values and context information. Instances are created by the plugin for one loading request and are only valid during the call they are passed to; do not keep or share them across threads.

Extension-point loader kind for values computed only from other attributes' values (and declared context), without looking at the item or the forest. The plugin can evaluate it wherever its dependencies are available: per item when all dependencies are item attributes, per row otherwise.

members.loadValue(com.almworks.jira.structure.ap: Computes the value from the dependency values obtained via the context. Returning null is treated as an undefined value (inside a composite, as 'not handled'). A runtime exception becomes an error value.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Context passed to an `ItemAttributeLoader` for one item. Instances are created by the plugin for one loading request and are only valid during the call they are passed to; do not keep or share them across threads.

members.getItemId(): Identity of the item whose value is being computed (the same as the loader's first argument). Never null.
members.getItem(Class): Resolves the current item to an object of the given class (for example Jira's `Issue` for issue items). Returns null if the item cannot be resolved (missing, or not visible to the plugin's resolver) or is not an instance of that class. Resolution happens at most once per item and uses items preloaded through `preload`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Extension-point loader kind for values that depend only on the item (and declared dependencies/context), not on where it appears in a structure. Values are cached per item. Implemented by plugins, usually via `AttributeLoaders.itemLoader`/`issueLoader`.

members.isItemTypeSupported(String): Whether the loader can compute values for items of the given item type (an item-type key such as `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue`). The plugin calls `loadValue` only for supported types; other items get an undefined value.
members.loadValue(com.almworks.jira.structure.ap: Computes the value for one item. Argument 1: the item (of a supported type). Argument 2: the context. Returning null means undefined (inside a composite, 'not handled'). A runtime exception becomes an error value.
members.preload(java.util.Collection, com.almwor: Called before a batch of `loadValue` calls with the ids of the items about to be loaded (only supported types), so the loader can fetch data in bulk. Default does nothing. The context here is the general context, not a per-item one.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Common super-interface of the loader kinds whose value for a row depends on other rows (aggregate, propagate, scanning). Such values are cached per forest and recalculated when the relevant part of the forest changes.

members.getCachingStrategy(): Defaults to `AttributeCachingStrategy.SHOULD`, because multi-row values are expensive to recompute.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Marker annotation (runtime-retained, for classes) placed on a value class. When the plugin's attribute-sensitivity setting is in its standard mode, attributes whose value format's value class carries this annotation are treated as not sensitive by default, i.e. they may be computed over rows the user cannot see. Marked internal: intended for the plugin's own value types.

Context passed to the per-child function returned by `PropagateAttributeLoader.loadChildren`, for one child row. Instances are created by the plugin for one loading request and are only valid during the call they are passed to; do not keep or share them across threads.

members.getIndex(): Zero-based position of the current row among its parent's children. Throws IllegalStateException if called outside a propagate calculation.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Context passed to `PropagateAttributeLoader.loadChildren`, describing the parent row whose children are about to be computed. Instances are created by the plugin for one loading request and are only valid during the call they are passed to; do not keep or share them across threads.

members.getChildren(): The parent's direct children in forest order; for the top level these are the forest's root rows. Never null.
members.getParent(): The parent row. For the forest's root rows it is the synthetic super-root row (row id -1). Null only when the loader is computing the value of the super-root itself (see `PropagateAttributeLoader.isLoadingSuperRoot`). Throws IllegalStateException outside a propagate calculation.
members.isLoadingSuperRoot(): True when the plugin is computing the value of the super-root itself (`getParent()` is null).
members.isLoadingRoots(): True when the children being computed are the forest's root rows (the parent is the super-root row, id -1).

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Extension-point loader kind for values that flow from parent to children (inherited values, paths, depths). The plugin processes the forest top-down: for each parent it calls `loadChildren` once with the parent's computed value and then applies the returned function to each child in order. Default caching strategy `SHOULD`.

members.loadChildren(com.almworks.jira.structure: Prepares the computation of a parent's children. Argument 1: the parent's value (undefined for root rows unless the loader computes a super-root value). Argument 2: the parent context. Returns a function taking a child row and its context and returning the child's value (a null result means undefined). Returning null from this method makes all these children undefined; a runtime exception makes them error values. The returned function is used only for this parent's children within the current request.
members.isLoadingSuperRoot(): Whether the loader also computes a value for the synthetic super-root above the roots; if so, the plugin first calls `loadChildren` with an undefined parent value and a null parent, applies the function to the super-root row, and passes that value as the parent value of the root rows. Default false.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Context for loaders that compute values for a row of a forest (single-row, aggregate, propagate and scanning loaders). Instances are created by the plugin for one loading request and are only valid during the call they are passed to; do not keep or share them across threads.

members.getRow(): The row whose value is being computed. Never null while a row is being processed.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Super-interface of the loader kinds that compute per-row values in a forest (single-row and the multi-row kinds). Values are cached per forest row.

members.preload(com.almworks.integers.LongSet, c: Called before a batch of rows is calculated so the loader can fetch data in bulk. Argument 1: ids of the rows about to be computed. Argument 2: the forest with its items. Argument 3: the general context. Default does nothing.
members.isWholeForestDependent(): True if the value of a row may change when anything in the forest changes (not only the row itself or the subtree/ancestors/preceding rows implied by the loader kind); the plugin then invalidates all values of the attribute on every forest change. Default false.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Context passed to a `ScanningAttributeLoader` for one row; adds information about the row's depth and the row that precedes it in forest order. Instances are created by the plugin for one loading request and are only valid during the call they are passed to; do not keep or share them across threads.

members.getDepth(): Depth of the current row: 0 for root rows, 1 for their children, and so on (a forest title row, if present, is not counted).
members.getPrecedingRow(): The row immediately before the current one in forest (depth-first) order, or null for the first row.
members.getPrecedingRowDepth(): Depth of the preceding row (same scale as `getDepth()`), or -1 if there is no preceding row.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Extension-point loader kind for values computed by scanning the forest in order, where each row's value depends on the preceding row's value (running totals, numbering). Default caching strategy `SHOULD`.

members.loadValue(com.almworks.jira.structure.ap: Computes the value of the current row. Argument 1: the value already computed for the preceding row in forest order (undefined for the first row; never null). Argument 2: the context. Returns the value; null means undefined; a runtime exception becomes an error value. The plugin does not call it for certain special rows, which get an undefined value.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Static factory methods that start the loader builders. Usually used through its subclass `AttributeLoaders`. Each call returns a new, independent, non-thread-safe builder.

members.itemLoader(com.almworks.jira.structure.a: Starts an item loader builder (`ItemAttributeLoaderBuilder`) for the spec, supporting all item types until `itemType` is called.
members.derivedLoader(com.almworks.jira.structur: Starts a derived loader builder with arbitrary dependencies (`DerivedAttributeLoaderBuilder`) for the spec.
Starts a builder for a derived loader computed from one dependency. Argument 1: the spec to compute. Argument 2: the dependency.
Starts a builder for a derived loader computed from two dependencies. Argument 1: the spec to compute. Arguments 2 and 3: the x and y dependencies.
members.constantLoader(com.almworks.jira.structu: Returns a derived loader builder, already complete, whose loader returns the given value (argument 2) for every row and item, with no dependencies. Call `build()` (other settings may still be added).
members.singleRowLoader(com.almworks.jira.struct: Starts a single-row loader builder (`SingleRowAttributeLoaderBuilder`) for the spec.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Context passed to a `SingleRowAttributeLoader`. Adds nothing to `RowAttributeContext`. Instances are created by the plugin for one loading request and are only valid during the call they are passed to; do not keep or share them across threads.
Extension-point loader kind for values that depend on the row itself (its item and row properties such as semantics or creator), but not on other rows. Values are cached per row.

members.loadValue(com.almworks.jira.structure.ap: Computes the value for the row (argument 1, the same as `context.getRow()`). Null means undefined (inside a composite, 'not handled'); a runtime exception becomes an error value.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: An immutable set of items, used as a trail: the items a value depends on, whose change must invalidate it. To stay small it may be stored imprecisely: up to a limit of 50 individual items it keeps the exact items; beyond that it keeps only their item types (matching every item of those types); beyond 10 types it becomes the set of all items. So `contains` may answer true for items that were never added, but never false for ones that were. The limits are read once from the plugin's dark-feature settings `structure.trail.itemLimit` and `structure.trail.typeLimit`. Instances come from the static factories and the `NONE`/`ALL_ITEMS` constants; the concrete subclasses are public only so that visitors can distinguish them. Immutable and thread-safe.

members.contains(com.almworks.jira.structure.api: True if a change to the given item is covered by this set (exactly, or by its item type, or because the set covers all items). False for null.
members.containsAny(java.util.Collection): True if `contains` is true for at least one item of the collection. False for a null or empty collection.
members.expand(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.i: Returns a set that also covers the given item (this set itself if already covered or if the item is null). May widen to item-type level or all items when limits are exceeded. Never null; this set is unchanged.
members.union(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.at: Returns a set covering everything in this set and in the argument; the argument may be null (returns this set). The result may be less precise (type level or all items) when the combined size exceeds the limits. Never null.
members.accept(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.a: Calls exactly one method of the visitor according to the set's form: `visitNone` for the empty set, `visit(OneItem)`, `visit(SpecificItems)`, `visit(OneType)`, `visit(SpecificTypes)`, or `visitAll`.
members.isEmpty(): True only for the empty set (`None`).
members.equals(Object): Two trail sets are equal when they have the same form and cover the same items, types, or all items.
members.hashCode(): Hash code consistent with `equals`, computed from the content (cached after the first call; never 0).
members.toString(): Debug text listing the content in braces, for example `{ALL}` or `{}`; the exact format is not a contract.
Creates a set of the given items; null elements are ignored. Empty input gives `None.NONE`; one distinct item gives a one-item set; up to the item limit an exact item set; more items are reduced to their item types (and, past the type limit, to `ALL_ITEMS`). A null array throws NullPointerException. Known defect: when the input contains nulls and exactly one distinct non-null item, the original returns a one-item set built from the first element of the input, which may be null (a set that then contains nothing).
members.of(java.util.Collection): Same as the varargs form for a collection; a null collection gives `None.NONE`. The same defect with a leading null element applies.
members.ofTypes(java.util.Collection): Creates a set covering all items of the given item types. Null elements are ignored; null or empty input gives `None.NONE`; one type gives a one-type set; past the type limit (10) the result is `ALL_ITEMS`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Form of `TrailItemSet` that covers every item; any change invalidates values with this trail. Use the `ALL_ITEMS` constant. Immutable and thread-safe.

members.ALL_ITEMS: The shared instance covering all items.
members.<init>(): Public by accident of the original declaration; do not call it. Use `ALL_ITEMS`: some union operations recognise the all-items set by identity with that constant, and a separate instance may make them fail.
members.union(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.at: Returns this set unchanged, whatever the argument.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: A read visitor that gathers the content of a trail set into plain Java sets; used for comparisons, hashing and printing. Obtain one with `collect`. The collector is mutable and not thread-safe; the sets it returns are its own mutable sets.

Creates a collector, lets the given set visit it, and returns it filled. The argument must not be null.
members.getTypes(): The item types collected from a type-level set, or null if the visited set had no types (empty, item-level, or all-items).
members.getItems(): The items collected from an item-level set, or null if the visited set had no individual items (empty, type-level, or all-items).
members.isAll(): True if the visited set covers all items.
members.visitItem(com.almworks.jira.structure.ap: Adds the item to the collected items. If the collector was prepared for a type-level set, an assertion fails when assertions are enabled; otherwise the item is still recorded.
members.visitType(String): Adds the item type to the collected types, with the same assertion behaviour as `visitItem` for a mismatching set.
members.visitAll(): Marks that all items are covered.
members.equals(Object): Equal to another collector with the same items, types and all-items flag.
members.toString(): Debug text: `{ALL}` for all items, otherwise the types and items joined by commas inside braces (the original always prints a separating comma, even when one side is empty). Not a contract.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Form of `TrailItemSet` that covers no items. Use the `NONE` constant. Immutable and thread-safe.

members.<init>(): Public by accident of the original declaration; do not call it. Use `NONE`: some union operations recognise the empty set by identity with that constant, and a separate instance may make them fail.
members.expand(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.i: Returns a one-item set with the given item, or this set if the item is null.
members.union(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.at: Returns the argument, or this set if the argument is null.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.attribut.summary: Form of `TrailItemSet` holding exactly one item. Created by the factories, not directly. Immutable and thread-safe.
